title: Rollout readiness mini-kit: metrics and trace checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, ops-friendly checklist and reference for shipping model/infra rollouts (hosted/dedicated/private). Focus is on the minimal telemetry and trace anchors we need to declare a rollout ‘ready’ and a short dashboard that helps oncall + SRE triage initial regressions during the first 48 hours.

Scope / constraints:
- Target: fast rollouts where we can’t fully instrument every edge case. Provide a small, high-value signal set that catches major regressions (latency, error, token-cost anomalies, cold-kvcache behavior).
- Intended consumers: oncall, release owner, SRE patch lead, solutions eng.
- Not a replacement for full signal taxonomy—this is the “first look” kit to fast-fail bad rollouts.

Quick SLI set (recommended):
- P99 response latency (end-to-end request->final-token emitted): slo candidate 99th <= 350ms for production small seq workloads; adjust by model class. Query name: inference.request.latency.p99_ms
- Error rate (user-facing failures): class = 4xx+5xx responses normalized by request count. inference.request.errors_pct
- Token generation throughput cost anomaly: tokens per minute per host and per-tenant; watch sudden token-per-request jumps. inference.tokens.per_request.rolling_p50
- KV-cache miss rate (warmth): fraction of requests that touch cold prefixes causing kv-cache fill paths. inference.kvcache.miss_rate
- Fallback fraction: % of requests routed to fallback model/region. routing.fallback.rate
- Synthetic probe success (canary): regular synthetic completions from a small prompt set (pass/fail + latency). synthetic.canary.health

Metric definitions / implementation notes:
- inference.request.latency.p99_ms: compute on server-side span that covers the full token generation flow (receive->emit-final). Tag with model, plan (hosted/dedicated), region, tenant_id (hashed). Rolling 5m and 1h windows. Store both p50/p95/p99.
- inference.request.errors_pct: increment for any request returning status != 200 (or success code from runtime). Expose error_type dimension (timeout, oom, model-unavailable, validation).
- inference.kvcache.miss_rate: define numerator = requests that trigger kvcache.load with cache_miss=true; denominator = total inference requests. Also track cold-prefix duration: time since last successful prefix hit for tenant.
- routing.fallback.rate: increment when the request executes the fallback code path (by policy). Include fallback_reason tag (capacity, model_regression, region_outage).
- synthetic.canary.health: probe job that runs N=5 short prompts every 1m. Store success boolean and latency. Keep last 24h timeseries.

Trace anchors (how to link traces to SLIs quickly):
- Anchor spans: http_receive -> auth -> routing_decision -> model_prepare -> kv_cache_op(s) -> model_infer -> token_emit -> http_respond.
- Key attributes for every span: trace_id, request_id, tenant_hash, model_name, model_version, plan_tier, region, host_id, tokens_expected (if present), kvcache_hit (boolean).
- Quick debug pattern: when p99 spikes, find top 20 traces by duration in the 5m window, group by span that inflates (model_infer vs kv_cache_op). If kv_cache_op dominates and miss_rate is high, check cold-prefix distribution by tenant.
- Sampling policy for early rollouts: increase trace sampling for requests tagged rollout=canary OR tenant in rollout cohort. Keep global adaptive sampling but ensure at least 1 trace/sec per service instance during rollout.

Dashboard skeleton (one-row checklist UI):
Panel 1: Rollout overview table\- rollout id, owner, start time, cohort size, hosts touched, current status (green/amber/red)\Panel 2: SLI widgets (sparklines + current value)\- latency p50/p95/p99, error rate %, kv-cache miss rate, fallback rate, synthetic canary pass rate\Panel 3: Top trace contributors (minimap + table)\- top spans by added latency, example trace ids (clickable)\Panel 4: Tenant heatmap (if multi-tenant)\- small multiple sparklines for top 10 tenants by traffic showing tok/request and p99\Panel 5: Investigation quicklinks\- runbook link, trace search prefilled query, synthetic probe logs (last 100), linked PR/Jira

Investigator quick-steps (6–8 minute triage):
1) Confirm whether the spike is global or cohort-specific: check rollout tag and per-region panels.\2) Open top trace contributors and identify which span type expanded. Model_infer -> model backend problem; kv_cache_op -> cold/cache-layer; token_emit -> downstream token transport.\3) Check fallback_rate and routing logs: if fallback increased, inspect policy reasons (capacity vs quality).\4) Look at recent deploy commit/PR for model change (linked PRs in dashboard).\5) If kv-cache miss surge: examine tenant-level cold-prefix durations, and check host evictions during window. Consider temporary autoscale/burst.\6) If error rate increased: examine error_type breakdown and full stack traces (request-level).\7) If synthetic canary failing: quarantine rollout, pause traffic, run curl-style probe against the failing model instance.

Rollout gating checklist (must pass or have mitigation):
- Observability: All recommended SLIs are present and graphed. (owner: release owner)\- Trace sampling bumped for rollout cohort (owner: eng-release)\- Synthetic canary green for 30m pre-rollout and 10m post initial rollout (owner: QA/Synthetics)\- KV-cache miss baseline measured and within 2x of control cohort (owner: infra)\- Auto-fallback config validated (owner: routing team)\- Pager/alert mapping exists for p99>threshold, errors>threshold, synthetic failure (owner: SRE)

Lightweight alerting proposals (for rollout):
- p99 latency increase > 2x baseline sustained 5m -> P1 oncall notification (pager)\- error rate > 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline -> P1 (unless known test spike)\- synthetic canary failing 3 consecutive probes -> P1 and auto-pause rollout\- kv-cache miss rate > 5% absolute jump -> P2 (investigate cache eviction/autoscale)

Open questions (to resolve before HQ rollout):
- What tenant anonymization/hashing policy do we want on the dashboard? (privacy vs triage fidelity)\- How long do we retain synthetic probe traces and full trace capture for cohort tenants? default 7d vs 30d? cost tradeoff.\- Do we want an emergency, manual-override to temporarily disable prefix-based kvcache eviction during rollouts?

Action items / next steps:
- Evan: add p99/end-to-end-span to the SLI collector (OBS-412) — due 2024-02-20\- Diego: create dashboard temp template and embed runbook links (PR in obs repo) — due 2024-02-22\- Priya: update trace sampling policy for rollout cohorts and validate in staging — due 2024-02-25

Notes to self / informal bits:
- Keep this small and operational: the goal is fast detection and cheap triage.\- On first rollout, expect noisy kv-cache churn; instrument host-level eviction logs to correlate host restarts with miss spikes.\- If rollout affects only small tenant subset, prefer targeted rollback vs global pause.

Useful queries / snippets (elastic/promql style - adapt to our stack):
- p99 latency (5m): quantile_over_time(0.99, inference_request_latency_ms{model=~".*"}[5m])\- kv-cache miss rate: sum(rate(inference_kvcache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m]))\- synthetic failure rate: sum(increase(synthetic_canary_failures_total[10m])) / sum(increase(synthetic_canary_total[10m]))

References / links:
- Linear ticket: OBS-412 (rollout SLI additions)\- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/229\- Runbook (work-in-progress): confluence.redwood/observability/rollout-runbook (link placeholder)

If you use this doc during a rollout, please paste the incident notes at the bottom so we can iterate.

-- Aisha
